context.note: ISSUE-FIXER's mechanism theory: Backfill.run/1 iterates Repo.all(Registration) -- ALL tenants, by design (that's its whole purpose per ISS-0332). Registry.register_type/2's resolve_schema_name(tenant_id) only checks the tenant_schemas REGISTRY ROW, not whether the physical Postgres schema still exists -- so if a tenant's schema is concurrently dropped (in tests: another async test's TenantFixture teardown running in the same partition process; in production: a genuine tenant-deprovisioning race with a backfill run) between resolve_schema_name/1's check and the subsequent EventType query, that query raises an uncaught error for a missing relation, crashing the whole Enum.reduce_while loop -- one stale/racing tenant takes down the entire backfill run instead of being skipped. This is a REAL production robustness gap this issue surfaces, not merely a test artifact -- design the fix at that level (Registry.register_type/2 or Backfill.run/1 tolerating a missing-schema tenant as a skip), not by changing test fixtures or narrowing Backfill.run/1's scope to a single tenant (that would defeat its stated purpose).

task.description: Design a fix per WF-03 Step 2. Claim this handoff by setting status to IN_PROGRESS only. Read lib/letflow/event_store/registry.ex's register_type/2 and resolve_schema_name/1 in full, and lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill.ex's run/1 in full, before designing. Write lib/letflow/design/iss0343-backfill-missing-schema-tolerance.md (design only, no implementation code) specifying: (a) how a missing/dropped schema is detected (which Postgrex/Ecto error shape to match on, e.g. Postgres error code 42P01 undefined_table -- verify the actual shape empirically by reading how other parts of this codebase already handle Postgrex errors, e.g. grep for '42P01' or 'UndefinedTable' or similar), (b) where the tolerance is added (register_type/2 itself, so every caller benefits, vs. only Backfill.run/1's call site), (c) what Backfill.run/1's counts map gains (e.g. a new :skipped_missing_schema count, or folding into existing :skipped), (d) whether this changes register_type/2's @spec (a new {:error, :tenant_schema_missing} tuple, or similar) and what call sites besides Backfill.run/1 need to handle it without crashing.
acceptance_criteria: the exact Postgrex/Ecto error shape to catch is specified, verified against how this codebase already handles similar DB errors elsewhere (cite the precedent)
the tolerance point (register_type/2 vs. Backfill.run/1's call site) is chosen with stated rationale
Backfill.run/1's result counts shape change (if any) is specified

register_type/2's @spec change (if any) is specified, and every other real call site of register_type/2 is checked and its handling of the new case (or lack of a change, if the tolerance is call-site-local to Backfill) is stated explicitly
